title: Core-based XRF Scanning Workflow for Mineralogical Variations in Clastic Reservoirs
author: Hussain, Al-Ramadan

steps.title: Obtain slabbed core plugs
steps.instruction: Collect slabbed rock‑core sections from the Ross Sandstone Formation, using split drill cores; each plug must be 20 mm high and match the 20 mm diameter of the Itrax scanner window, noting clay‑rich and clay‑poor intervals.

steps.title: Set up XRF scanner parameters
steps.instruction: Mount the core on the Itrax scanner and move it continuously past a 20 mm wide, 0.2 mm thick molybdenum (Mo) beam with an 8 mm wide nozzle detector; operate the instrument at 30 kV and 50 mA, using a count time of 15 s per point and a step size of 200 µm. Beam penetration is a few microns for light elements up to ~100 µm for heavy elements.

steps.title: Acquire raw XRF intensity data
steps.instruction: Record major and trace element intensities along the entire core length, integrating optical images to align obvious core breaks (visible as backsteps in the elemental profiles) and ensuring continuous data acquisition.

steps.title: Process raw spectra with Q‑Spec
steps.instruction: Open the Q‑Spec spectral analysis software, select the desired elements for extraction, remove any spurious or unnecessary elemental choices, adjust fitting parameters as needed, and run batch‑controlled post‑processing to generate cleaned intensity datasets.

steps.title: Collect co‑located calibration plugs
steps.instruction: From the same 20 mm high window used for scanning, extract 19 representative bulk‑rock plug samples for quantitative geochemical calibration.

steps.title: Prepare powder for ICP‑AES
steps.instruction: For each plug, weigh 0.2 g of homogenized powder, add 0.9 g of a lithium metaborate/lithium tetraborate flux mixture, and mix thoroughly in a crucible.

steps.title: Fuse powders
steps.instruction: Place the mixture in a furnace and fuse at 1000 °C until a homogeneous melt forms; then allow the melt to cool and solidify.

steps.title: Dissolve fused melt
steps.instruction: Dissolve the cooled melt in 100 mL of an acid solution containing 4 % nitric acid (HNO₃) and 2 % hydrochloric acid (HCl).

steps.title: Perform ICP‑AES analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the dissolved solutions by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP‑AES), correct for any spectral inter‑element interferences, and calculate oxide (wt %) and trace element (ppm) concentrations.

steps.title: Compute log‑ratio calibration equations
steps.instruction: Convert both Itrax intensity data and ICP‑AES concentrations to additive log‑ratio (alr) form, calculate log‑ratios for element pairs (Si/K, Ca/K, Fe/K, Ti/K, Zr/K), perform regression analysis to obtain LRCEs, and select potassium (K) as the optimal denominator because it yields the highest R² values (typically >0.95; K₂O R² = 0.93). Note that the high R² values reflect minimal calibration issues due to the simple quartz‑rich composition, low porosity (<1 %), smooth cut surfaces, and absence of interstitial fluids.

steps.title: Apply calibration to XRF data
steps.instruction: Use the LRCE coefficients to transform raw Itrax intensities into calibrated elemental concentrations (e.g., K₂O, Si/K, Ca/K, Fe/K), generating continuous, quantitative profiles along the core.

steps.title: Interpret calibrated profiles
steps.instruction: Examine calibrated log‑ratio curves: log(Si/K) decreasing upward indicates increasing illite/mica; K₂O mirroring log(Si/K) confirms illite content; log(Ca/K) bow‑shaped trend marks diagenetic calcite cement; log(Fe/K) decreasing upward reflects chlorite variation. Identify lithological changes such as mud‑clast‑rich versus mud‑clast‑poor intervals, noting that Itrax provides high‑resolution detail not captured by conventional petrography.
